item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This is just a collection of gross acts strung together by randomness-in-place-of humour. There's a few comedic through-lines which seem to possess some principle of humour (like the slogan-shouting or the Kate Bush monologue) but even those didn't actually strike me as funny.

While I didn't recoil in disgust, I didn't laugh either, and I found the piece oddly unwholesome. I'm made slightly uneasy by the repeated focus on doing nasty things to young Chinese women (in a way that foregrounds their age, race and gender, no less) as something that is for some reason particularly hilarious. To be honest, this puts me off the piece to the point where I'd probably downvote even if it were a coherent joke (which it never quite manages to be).

I can't imagine this took that much effort to think up, and it shows.

item.content:encoded:
But then, it's still a matter of opinion, because in my view SCP-WTF-J is just that

The key phrase you are missing is "mainlist articles or serious tales", this is a -J so we aren't meant to try to imagine this with suspension of disbelief. If you want to imagine this in-universe, imagine that someone attached to SCP-2845 wrote this as a frustratred parody.

The difference is that I am being asked to suspend disbelief for this no more than I am for the chicken crossing the road, whereas lolFoundation asks for the same level of SoD as does any speculative fiction, and then proceeds to append wacky hijinks to a classified document about a world swallowing horror and expects me to take it seriously.

This is a joke. The whole point is that it's ridiculous and impossible. It's a parody of SCP-2845. Absolutely nothing here is meant to be thought of as serious.

I don't know how there's this cognitive disconnect with you. Do you think SCP-___-J or SCP-999-J are meant to be thought of as canon and serious? No, you're supposed to either laugh or not laugh, vote accordingly, and move on.

I'm not trying to sound condescending, so if I am, I apologize. But I think you're over-thinking it.
